properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 22 at 3:10PM CST until November 22 at 3:30PM CST by NWS Little Rock AR
properties.description:
At 310 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm was located over Poyen, or 11
miles west of Sheridan, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Prattsville...                    Poyen...
Jenkins Ferry State Park...       Buie...
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued November 22 at 4:59PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...

* At 459 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. These strong
thunderstorms were located over open waters of Atlantic Waters of
Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N zone, moving north at 15
knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from
10 NM to 19.5N.
properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.
properties.area: Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico AND USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 22 at 3:47PM EST until November 22 at 5:45PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
SMWMHX

The National Weather Service in Newport has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Cape Hatteras to Ocracoke Inlet NC from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Ocracoke Inlet to Cape Lookout NC from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 545 PM EST.

* At 347 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 27 nm southeast of Atlas Tanker, moving
northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts to 40 knots, high waves, dangerous lightning, and heavy
rain are possible with this storm.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.area: Waters from Cape Hatteras to Ocracoke Inlet NC from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Ocracoke Inlet to Cape Lookout NC from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 2:42PM CST until November 22 at 5:45PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:

* WHERE...Southwestern Aransas County in south central Texas...
Eastern San Patricio County in south central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Portland, Taft, Gregory and Taft Southwest.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 22 at 2:56PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to
reach 5.3 feet and Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
continue a gradual rise through the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 5.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM EST Sunday was 5.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising in Major
Flood Stage through the week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EST.

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

forecast to climb into Major Flood stage around mid-week.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 7.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM EST Sunday was 7.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue a steady rise,
reaching 8.2 feet this week. Additional rises are possible
thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 22 at 2:46PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to reach Major Flood Stage, well above its previous record
flood stage. The river level will remain steady into the middle of
next week, with a chance for the start of a slow decline late in the
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring is forecast. This will set an
all time flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM EST Sunday the stage was 18.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:15 PM EST Sunday was 18.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage and well above the previous record stage at 18.7 feet
through this weekend into early next week. The start of a slow
decline may be possible late this week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 22 at 2:39PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to hold steady early this week, then slowly rise
mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Sunday was 4.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to hold steady near 4.1 feet
early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage
forecast mid to late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying

an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached

warned area.

Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
